topic: Microsoft AI-300 exam preparation - Operationalizing Machine Learning and Generative AI Solutions - the 2026 Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) Engineer Associate certification covering MLOps and GenAIOps on Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry
cert_name: Microsoft Certified: Machine Learning Operations Engineer Associate
exam_format: Approximately 40-60 questions, ~100 minutes, passing score 700/1000, online proctored or test center. Question types include multiple choice, multiple select, drag-and-drop, build-list/ordering, case studies, and hot area. Associate-level certification renews annually via a free online assessment on Microsoft Learn. Exam released in 2026 (beta early 2026, generally available May 2026).
question_types: multiple choice (single answer, exactly 4 options) and multiple select clearly marked as 'Select TWO/THREE'
audience: MLOps and GenAIOps engineers, ML engineers, data scientists moving into production, and DevOps engineers expanding into AI. Candidates should have Python experience, an entry-level understanding of DevOps (GitHub Actions, CLIs), and hands-on time with Azure Machine Learning and Microsoft Foundry. A strong next step after AI-102/AI-103 or the Azure Data Scientist track, and a complement to the NVIDIA NCP-AIO AI-operations course.
author: Aseem Mankotia

domains.name: Design and implement an MLOps infrastructure
domains.notes: Create and manage resources in an Azure Machine Learning workspace: workspaces, datastores, compute targets, and identity/access management for workspaces. Create and manage assets: data assets, environments, components, and sharing assets across workspaces using registries. Implement Infrastructure as Code (IaC) for Machine Learning: configure GitHub integration for secure access; deploy workspaces and resources with Bicep and the Azure CLI; automate resource provisioning with GitHub Actions workflows; restrict network access to workspaces; and manage source control for ML projects with Git. Foundation domain - establish the reproducible, governed platform everything else runs on.

domains.name: Implement machine learning model lifecycle and operations
domains.notes: The largest domain. Orchestrate model training: experiment tracking with MLflow, automated ML (AutoML) for model exploration, notebooks for experimentation, automated hyperparameter tuning, running training scripts, distributed training for large/deep-learning models, training pipelines, and comparing model performance across jobs. Model registration and versioning: package a feature-retrieval spec with the model artifact, register an MLflow model, evaluate models with Responsible AI principles, and manage model lifecycle including archiving. Deploy models for production: real-time vs batch endpoints with managed inference, testing and troubleshooting endpoints, and progressive rollout plus safe rollback strategies. Monitor and maintain in production: detect and analyze data drift, monitor performance metrics, and configure retraining or alert triggers when thresholds are exceeded.

domains.name: Design and implement a GenAIOps infrastructure
domains.notes: Microsoft Foundry environments and platform configuration: create/configure Foundry resources and project environments; identity and access management with managed identities and RBAC; network security and private networking; and IaC deployment with Bicep and the Azure CLI. Deploy and manage foundation models for production: serverless API endpoints vs managed compute, selecting the right model for a use case, model versioning and production deployment strategies, and configuring provisioned throughput units (PTUs) for high-volume workloads. Prompt versioning and management with source control: designing and developing prompts, creating prompt variants and comparing performance, and version-controlling prompts in Git repositories. This is the generative-AI counterpart to the classic MLOps platform domain.

domains.name: Implement generative AI quality assurance and observability
domains.notes: Configure evaluation and validation for generative AI applications and agents: build test datasets and data mapping for comprehensive evaluation; implement AI quality metrics including groundedness, relevance, coherence, and fluency; configure risk and safety evaluations for harmful-content detection; and set up automated evaluation workflows using built-in and custom metrics. Implement observability for generative AI apps and agents: continuous monitoring in Foundry; monitor latency, throughput, and response times; track and optimize cost metrics including token consumption and resource usage; and configure detailed logging, tracing, and debugging for production troubleshooting. Emphasis on catching quality/safety regressions before and after deployment.

domains.name: Optimize generative AI systems and model performance
domains.notes: Optimize retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) performance and accuracy: tune similarity thresholds, chunk sizes, and retrieval strategies; select and fine-tune embedding models for domain-specific accuracy; implement and optimize hybrid search combining semantic and keyword retrieval; and evaluate/improve RAG with relevance metrics and A/B testing frameworks. Implement advanced fine-tuning and model customization: design and implement advanced fine-tuning methods, create and manage synthetic data for fine-tuning, monitor and optimize fine-tuned model performance, and manage a fine-tuned model from development through production deployment. The 'make it faster, cheaper, and more accurate' domain.

extra_guidance: AI-300 is a brand-new 2026 certification (beta early 2026, GA May 2026), so Udemy competition is thin - marketing angle: 'first-to-market, built for the NEW AI-300' and 'the production/operations cert that sits on top of AI-102/AI-103.' The exam title is 'Operationalizing Machine Learning and Generative AI Solutions'; the credential name is 'Machine Learning Operations Engineer Associate.' The five domain names and weights above are Microsoft's official skills-measured outline (study guide last updated 2026-03-05) - use them verbatim. This is an ADVANCED, hands-on engineering exam that spans BOTH worlds: classic MLOps on Azure Machine Learning (MLflow, AutoML, pipelines, real-time/batch endpoints, data drift) AND GenAIOps on Microsoft Foundry (foundation-model deployment, PTUs, prompt versioning, evaluation, observability, RAG optimization, fine-tuning). Do not let it drift into being another 'intro to Azure AI' course - assume the learner already knows what a model and a prompt are; teach how to OPERATIONALIZE them. Tooling to cover concretely at read-and-understand level: Azure ML SDK/CLI v2, MLflow, Bicep, Azure CLI, GitHub Actions, managed identities/RBAC, private endpoints, Foundry evaluation and tracing. Labs: provision an Azure ML workspace with Bicep + GitHub Actions, register and version an MLflow model, deploy to a managed online endpoint with blue/green rollout, configure data-drift monitoring, deploy a foundation model to a serverless endpoint, wire up prompt version control, and run a groundedness/safety evaluation in Foundry. Practice tests must be scenario/case-study heavy: choosing real-time vs batch endpoints, serverless vs managed compute, PTU sizing, semantic vs hybrid retrieval tuning, when to fine-tune vs optimize RAG, safe rollout/rollback design, and diagnosing drift or grounding regressions. Cover classic traps: managed identity vs keys, Bicep vs ARM/portal, online vs batch endpoints, MLflow model vs custom, groundedness vs relevance vs coherence metrics, and provisioned throughput vs pay-as-you-go. Final chapter must be a full exam simulation walkthrough with a 100-minute time-management strategy including case-study pacing.
